sense.text:
“Casting all your care upon him”: we must cast all our cares upon God. When things get bad and you are hurting inside, when you are sick or in the hospital and the doctor has told you that you might not have long to live, we as a people have to learn to cast all our cares upon the Lord. That is the state of mind to have.

“For he careth for you.” No matter what we are going through, no matter how hard it is, even in sickness and in death, the Lord cares for us. Even in death the Lord cares for you. Don't think death is the end of it.

precepts.why:
“In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul.” That is where your comfort comes from. When you are sick, when you are dealing with depression or whatever bad you are going through in your life, we have to learn to comfort ourselves, and this shows where that comfort comes from: the thoughts within.

You will be by yourself while you are afflicted and going through your trials and tribulations, whether in prison, or sick at home with all the brothers and sisters gone, or with the doctor telling you that you don't have long to live. All you have is your thoughts. So how do you comfort yourself in your thoughts? You have to know the scriptures and understand the scriptures. You trust in the Lord and you comfort yourself through the scriptures.

Bad things are going to happen to all of us. Some will get sick, some will be put in prison, some will lose loved ones. This is how we comfort ourselves in our thoughts: “I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.” The brothers and sisters that die, we shouldn't be sorrowful for them. If you die in Christ you are not like others that have no hope.

“For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.” If you die right now and you are doing what's right, you are not really dead. The Lord is going to bring you back. You are living right, you believe in Christ: you are coming back. That is the thought to hold when the doctor says you don't have long to live: I have been serving God and doing what's right, I am going to be back, and this is not the end of it for me.

A lot of us look at death as a bad thing. But every last one of us has to leave this flesh; death comes to all men, by sickness, by accident, however the Lord chooses to take you out. The comfort is to put all your trust in the Lord and to understand that when you leave this world you are going to be with the Lord. It's not that you die; you leave this wicked world and go back to the Lord. That is what death really is.

Read with verse 13, them that die, “that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope”: don't sorrow like people that don't have hope, because those of us that die in Christ have hope. Then: “Wherefore comfort one another with these words.”

These words, the word of God, are the thoughts you need to comfort you when you are by yourself going through what you are going through. The teachers will not be around you all the time or on the phone with you all the time. Sometimes you might get depressed, sometimes you might feel like giving up, and Satan is going to be whispering in your ears: God don't care about you, why is God allowing you to die? You have to learn to use the word of God to find comfort and comfort yourself with these words.

“Seeing his days are determined”: every one of us must understand that our days on this earth are determined with God. “The number of his months are with thee”: the amount of months God gives you on this earth is with him. “Thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass”: there is a day and an hour that every last one of us has to die, already ordained by God, and we cannot pass that bound. If God says you are not going to see 2027, you are not going to see 2027. Yet if the people fast and pray and really go in, the Lord could say, I'm going to give him another 5 or 10 years. But every man has a bound amount of time on this earth and will not go past it.

“Turn from him, that he may rest”: we go back to paradise. The same way the Lord rested on the seventh day, that rest is us going back to paradise if we are righteous.

“Till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.” A hireling is somebody you give work to for a certain amount of time. God sends us on this earth with a job to do and a certain amount of time to do it, and once the job is finished and the time is up, he takes you back. He did the same with Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David and all our forefathers, with Judah Maccabees and his brothers, and with Elijah. God has a purpose and a job for every last one of us, and sends us here as hirelings for a time.

“For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again”: that tree is our hope for immortality, to be gone over another day.

So whether it is prison, persecution or sickness, we have to put all our trust in the Lord and let these scriptures comfort us. Don't let your thoughts depress you and put fear on you when you are by yourself. Comfort yourself: I'm going to see the Lord, I've been keeping the commandments, and if I live or I die I'm with the Lord.

This is what Paul said: “For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.” Some of you are sick, and the doctor might say you don't have long to live. The way you look at death is not what you think it is. If you die, you are with the Lord.

This is the mindset we must have: whether we live or die we belong to the Lord. Don't let fear of things mess with your spirit. We have to build ourselves up so we are not afraid of being with the Lord. When you think like this you are putting all your trust in the Lord. We are all given a certain time on this earth; we are all hirelings.

“We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body”: we are willing and confident to die, to leave this body, this flesh we are in, that we suffer in and are sick in. We all have to bring our minds to this form of thinking. “And to be present with the Lord”: once we leave this body we are going to be present with the Lord. That is the confidence to have. Don't be afraid of death. Death for us is not what it is for everyone else that has no hope.

“Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.” We want to be accepted. That is why you have to keep the commandments, love each other and do what's right. The labour is doing what's right on this earth, so that you can be in his presence when you die.

And even though you die and go to paradise, the Lord is bringing you back on this earth. The kingdom of heaven is God's kingdom coming on this earth and us ruling this earth. Don't have the state of mind that you are going to live up in the sky. God's kingdom coming on earth is the whole end of everything.

sense.text: “I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” He is the God of the living, so Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are living. They are not dead. This is part of the comfort for the brothers and sisters going through sickness and facing death.

precepts.why:
This shows why Christ said what he said. “And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons”: this is after he blessed his twelve sons and let them know what was going to happen to them in the last days. “He gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost”: he died. Then: “and was gathered unto his people.”

When Jacob died he was gathered unto his people. That is saying what Christ is saying: he is not the God of the dead but of the living. Jacob was gathered unto his people in paradise. He wasn't really dead; he went back to paradise. That is the hope and the comfort the brothers and sisters must have.

Which people was Jacob gathered unto after he died? “For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named”. The whole family, in heaven and in earth.

That family in heaven and earth is named Israel, a prince that has power with God. So when it says he was gathered unto his people, it means he went to paradise, to his people there.

sense.text: “They shall come all for violence”: when the white man came to America he came for violence. He came, he murdered, he killed and he took. “And they shall gather the captivity as the sand”: the captivity is the 12 tribes of Israel.

“And they shall scoff at the kings”: they scoffed at our kings, saying, who the hell is you, we don't respect you, and they enslaved our kings. “And the princes shall be a scorn unto them”: our princes, the chiefs here in America, in Puerto Rico, in all these lands and in Africa, were a scorn unto them.

“They shall deride every strong hold”: every city and every stronghold in America, in the western hemisphere, was taken by the white man, whether of the Aztecs, the Mayans or the Incas, the Zulu tribe or the Ashanti tribe in Africa, or the North American Indians. “For they shall heap dust, and take it”: they cause confusion and take it.

“Then shall his mind change”: after he has murdered and killed and taken every stronghold, he changes his mind. “Imputing this his power unto his god”: he starts teaching Christianity. He says In God we trust, God bless America, a Christian, God-fearing country, after he murdered, killed, looted and stole; everything he has, that is how he got it. And he imputes it unto the power of his god, the white image of Christ.

When and why did his mind change? After 1945, when America and Europe became the superpower of the earth. America did not look good in how it was treating the black people living here: segregation, treating us like crap, while talking about justice in the earth and what Russia and other countries were doing. The other countries said, you have no moral standing, look how you are treating the black slaves in your country. There was no way America and Europe could push democracy in Africa and all over the world, acting like a loving, God-fearing people about rights and justice, while segregation and the Jim Crow laws were still set up here. Those laws were named after Jim Crow, a white man in blackface mocking black people as buffoonish and unworthy of equal rights, and they segregated our people in education, transportation, housing and public facilities, and kept us from voting with poll taxes, literacy tests and grandfather clauses. They said they let us go from slavery, but that was oppression; we were not free and did not have equal rights.

So he had to change his image: I'm going to oppress you Negroes, but I'm going to do it in a slick way, not openly for the world. That is what happened in 1965 when we got civil rights. It was not because the white man loved you or because Lyndon B. Johnson loved you; there is a quote where he said that if they gave black people civil rights they would have them voting Democrat for the next 100 years. His mind changed because of world opinion and because he became the world superpower.

“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us”. What is this hell and death we made a covenant with? Habakkuk speaks of America, and hell and death follow them. It is the shadow of Egypt; it is America. Our people made a covenant with America in 1964, when we entered into the whole civil rights and integration. Martin Luther King understood it, and that is why he was killed: he said, I integrated my people into a burning house.

When Christ was on the earth our people did the same. The hell and death back then was Rome; when Christ said the gates of hell would not prevail against the church, he was speaking of Rome. Our forefathers made a covenant with Rome when they said they had no king but Caesar. It is the same state of mind our people have today: they love voting for US presidents, they love this system and trust in it. And the same way the Pharisees and our people were destroyed in 70 AD after that covenant with Rome, the same thing is going to happen to our people here in America that made that covenant with America. There is a book about the covenant with black America, which Bishop Yasha once mentioned. It has been 60 plus years since that covenant and civil rights, and nothing has changed; it is going backwards.

They think they will not be destroyed when the overflowing scourge comes. “For we have made lies our refuge”: making the covenant with death means making lies your refuge. Lies like Jesus Christ is a white man; Easter and Christmas; that the people in that land are the Jews. All of that is part of the covenant our people made with hell and death. “And under falsehood have we hid ourselves.”

“Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone”: that tried stone is Christ. “A precious corner stone”: he is the cornerstone. “A sure foundation”: he is the foundation. “He that believeth shall not make haste.”

“Judgment also will I lay to the line”: the line is the plumb line, a tool used to build a house or a wall. “And righteousness to the plummet”: that wall is going to be built straight and right, the church of Christ built right.

“And the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies”: the hail is destruction. It will sweep away all the lies that have been taught on the earth and that our people trust in: Christ born December 25th, Easter, white Jesus, all the Christian lies. They will be swept away by Christ and by the men building the church. The line also goes into teachings, going out to the ends of the earth: we are going to tear down all the lies and falsehood our people trust in with the word of God.

“And the waters shall overflow the hiding place”: the waters are the word of God, and the hiding place is all the lies and the things they have been hiding. The word of God is going to reveal every secret thing they are doing and have done, and every lie they tell.

“And your covenant with death shall be disannulled”: the covenant the blacks in America made with America in 1964-65, the civil rights, the Voting Rights Act, integration, all the things our people trust in. All of it is going to fall apart, and that is what Trump is doing right now. The same way the covenant we made with Rome was disannulled after a time, and Rome came and destroyed us, it is going to be the same here in America. It has been 60 years since the leaders of our people made a covenant with America.

“And your agreement with hell shall not stand”: all that civil rights stuff our people signed and trust in is not going to stand. It is all falling apart before our eyes. “When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it”: trodden down right here in the streets of America. Bad things are coming to this place; judgments are coming.

Trump told the Christians, vote this one time and in four years you won't have to vote again, we'll have it fixed. Those Christians are the same Christians of the 1700s and 1800s that had sheets over their heads lynching us. And now you see him fulfilling it: black voters purged from the rolls by the million, a 92-year-old cousin of Dr. Martin Luther King denied her vote, the Supreme Court voting six to three to strike down the Voting Rights Act, black districts redrawn, the SAVE America Act demanding a passport to vote while the libraries where poor people got their passports are shut down and passports are taken over child support, marijuana rescheduled while driving high becomes a felony so you cannot vote, black officials fired across the government, the only black governor uninvited from the governors' meeting he chairs, nursing declassified as a profession, black history taken out of the schools, the plaques telling of the nine people George Washington held as slaves in the President's House taken down at Trump's command, and prisoners in Alabama worked for free, two dollars a day, because the 13th Amendment lets a man be made a slave once he is convicted of a crime: slavery is alive till this day. That is Jim Crow again.

Affirmative action and DEI were brought about because of Jim Crow: we had no equal rights, and we would go for a job overqualified and not be hired. Now Trump is getting rid of all of it. Make America great again means make America white again. Many brothers and sisters still say, this is my country, I'm an American; but you are going to see the racism of America and of the white man, and come to understand that these people hate you. Negroes are in an uproar that their voting rights are being taken away, and that is good for them, because God said that covenant is going to be disannulled, and that is what is taking place.

And all the immigrants living here have rights because of Judah, because of that fight in the '60s for civil rights. Judah is an old lion right now, but the spirit of Christ is rising him up, and Judah is roaring.

precepts.why:
Two chapters on, the covenant is named. “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me”: we made a covenant with somebody, but not with the Lord. “And that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”: that covering is Christianity and politics, Democrats and Republicans. “That they may add sin to sin”: that is what these religions do, saying you don't have to keep God's laws anymore, and that is what politics does.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth”: back then we literally went down to ancient Egypt for help, when God told Jeremiah to tell the people not to go down to Egypt to run away from Babylon. That is the literal history, but there is a double meaning. “To strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” The shadow of Egypt is America that our people trust in. A shadow is not the real thing; it is a reflection of the real thing. America is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, so trusting in the shadow of Egypt is our people trusting in America. That is the covenant with hell and death.

And this is what God says about that trust: “Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.” We will be ashamed of having our strength in Pharaoh, the presidents of America, all who vote for them, and it is going to be our people's confusion. They are going to say, why?

“Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest”. Because of the covenant our people made with America, with hell and death, our people have been at rest. You think this place is your rest. Our people have been rocked to sleep, trusting in lies and falsehoods, fed democracy and the American dream.

But God says arise and depart: this place is not your rest, “because it is polluted”. This whole land is polluted. “It shall destroy you.”

Jesse Jackson, one of the architects of civil rights and one of the leaders that made the covenant with hell and death, said: we must never surrender, America will get better and better, keep hope alive. He was telling us to trust in America. But see what the Bible says.

“Turn you to the strong hold”: God warned us to turn to the stronghold. He does not want us to trust in America. The stronghold is our God, and we find our God in the scriptures. “Ye prisoners of hope”: we are prisoners of hope because we are always hoping, the same thing Jesse Jackson said, keep hope alive, things are going to get better. That is why the sister wept when she could not vote and said it was not her country: she is a prisoner of hope.

Is it getting better? No, it is getting worse. Why? Because God said that the covenant our leaders made with America, with hell and death, is not going to stand.

sense.text:
“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help”: we are always looking for help, vain help. “In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” Our people came here as slaves in America, and we look to the people that oppress us and destroy us to save us: give us rights, treat us as human beings. Let's vote for a president, let's vote for a senator that could better our community. That is how our people think. We look for a nation that cannot save us.

The scripture tells you who is going to save you. Your saviour is your king, your leader, your governor. Your saviour is Christ, the black Messiah.

“Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee”: the throne of iniquity is the so-called white man, and they are not going to have fellowship with the Lord. “Which frameth mischief by a law?” They frame mischief by law: all these laws they are setting up are to destroy our people and take away the rights you got here in Babylon, to stop you from voting, to lock you up and put you in prison. Under the Jim Crow laws, if you went against them you were locked up and put in prison, and our people were getting their ass whooped.

That covenant you made with America is disannulling; that is what is going on right now. Because we trust in America and this system and don't turn to our stronghold and trust in our God, all the things we trust in are going to disappear. The Lord is taking all of it away.
“The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful.” In 1965 we made a covenant with hell and death, with America, with the vile person that calls himself a liberal.

“For the vile person will speak villany”: what the liberal speaks is villainy. How many think the Democrats love you? The Democrats are the villains too, and no defense from the Republicans. “And his heart will work iniquity, to practise hypocrisy”: they are hypocrites. They say, we love black people, and then they sign laws and set things up to destroy our people. They come into the black community promising to do this and that, sell you a lie, and you believe them.

“And to utter error against the Lord”: the things they tell you to do are error against God, and you err against God following these liberals, these Democrats. “To make empty the soul of the hungry”: following the Democrats we are not being fed with the word of God. “And he will cause the drink of the thirsty to fail”: our people are thirsty for the word of God, thirsty for truth, and they cause it to fail.

“The instruments also of the churl are evil”: the instruments are Section 8, where the father is not in the house, welfare, food stamps, the independent woman, a woman don't need a man, homosexuality, transgender, abortion. All of these the liberals push, and all of it is evil.

“He deviseth wicked devices”: the devices are the things he comes up with and sells to our people, and one of them is civil rights, the covenant you made with them. There is no such thing as integration; we were not integrated with America, we assimilated among them. That is why you see women running around with green eyes and blonde hair. We don't own our own farms, our own businesses or our own banks anymore. We own nothing. That is what they did in '65: the Democrats took away your power. Civil rights was not good for our people. “To destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.”
“But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand.” That is the wicked stuff they stand on.

“Rise up, ye women that are at ease”: God says this because it is the black women in America that profit from these liberal things. All the things the liberals set up are for the black woman, not the black man, to keep the house divided: Section 8 and food stamps, but make sure the man is not around; be independent, you don't need a man, be a career woman. They put all these liberal things in the women's minds. God says rise up because all these liberal things are going to fail: over 200,000 women with high-paying positions in the federal government lost their jobs. Rise up, you black women at ease here in America, who think America is your rest.

“Hear my voice”: listen to God's word. Don't worry about the voice of the man reading it; it is the word of God you are hearing right now, you black women in America that are comfortable here. “Ye careless daughters”: you live carelessly, sex here and there, three or four baby daddies all on child support, taking a percentage from each one. All of that is going to fail; even child support is going to be cut off soon.

“Give ear unto my speech”: the time is coming, and it is right now, where the black woman is going to listen to God's speech and to the men of God as they teach this word.

“Many days and years shall ye be troubled”: affliction is coming here in America, here in Babylon. All the liberal things the black woman got, all the rights the white man gave you, the voting rights, the career the white man told you to have instead of your kids and your family, you are going to lose all of it. The sisters who got government funding to become nurses, to build a career and buy a house: that is done. Trouble is coming here.

“I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence”: God went and returned to his place. Our people have not acknowledged their offences yet, but we are beginning to, and that is why you see us coming together. “And seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Affliction is coming here in America and all over the world. God says that for his people to seek him and seek his face, he has to afflict them. All the liberal things are going to fail, the covenant we made with America in 1965 is going to disannul, and oppression and affliction will rise up on our people living in America, so that we turn to our God.

It has been 60 years since you got civil rights. What did you black people do with your civil rights? You made rap music about killing each other, you became drug dealers, you are murdering and killing each other and hating each other. Since the white man let you out of slavery and Jim Crow, that is what you did. And the white man said, the hell with that, I'm taking away all them rights I gave you niggers. That is what you see Trump doing. God sent Trump to do what you see him doing, because he wants you to turn to him.

“Gather yourselves together”: everything you see taking place, the affliction rising on our people, is going to force us to gather together on an even higher level than you see now. As affliction comes down, our people lose the false sense of security they thought they had, and a lot of our people are going to seek God's face and turn to the stronghold. That is the gathering together. As Jim Crow comes back, our people are going to start separating and gathering together, doing things on our own for ourselves, learning to love each other, deal right with each other, work together and get things done. That is what bringing back Jim Crow is going to do. Don't be mad that they are bringing back Jim Crow and taking the voting rights; there is a law behind it.

“Yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: the nations don't desire us. They say, we don't want you to vote in our elections. They got rid of the civil rights acts, and Trump brought back segregation on the federal level, letting federal contractors have segregated bathrooms. We are not desired. The Lord does not want us to assimilate with them; he wants us to gather together, so he is making it where they kick us out of all their systems and all the benefits they have given us for the last 60 years.

What they did is one step closer to civil war, not Negroes against whites, but Democrats against Republicans. The Most High is setting up the stage for them to fight against each other.
